Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:10:1.hebrew: פטור - מכרת, דלא אתי איסור יום כפורים ומיחל אאיסור נבילה דקדים. אם נתנבלה מערב יום כפורים, הרי קדם איסור נבלה; ואם נתנבלה ביום כפורים, אפי' הכי אסורה היתה עליו מבערב משום אבר מן החי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:10:1.english: Exempt - From karet, for the prohibition of Yom Kippur does not come and take effect upon the prohibition of a carcass, which preceded [it]. If it became a carcass before Yom Kippur, behold, the prohibition of a carcass preceded [it]; and if it became a carcass on Yom Kippur, even so, it was forbidden to him from the [previous] evening due to [the prohibition of] a limb from a living animal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:11:1.hebrew: איסור חמור על איסור קל - יום כפורים שהוא בכרת, על איסור נבילה שהוא בלאו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:11:1.english: A severe prohibition upon a lenient prohibition - [Such as the prohibition of] Yom Kippur, which carries [the penalty of] karet, upon the prohibition of [an unslaughtered] carcass [neveilah], which is [subject to] a negative commandment:

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:11:2.hebrew: אבל איסור קל כו' - כגון אלמנה לכהן גדול על איסור אחותו, שהיא בכרת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:11:2.english: But a light prohibition etc. - For example, [the prohibition of] a widow to a High Priest [taking effect] upon the prohibition of his sister, which is [punishable] by karet [excision].

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:12:1.hebrew: ואיכא דאמרי הא מני - דאיצטריך ליה למילף, דלא ליחול איסור אלמנה לכ"ג על איסור אחותו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:12:1.english: And there are those who say: In accordance with whose [opinion] is this? - For it was necessary for [the tanna] to derive that the prohibition of a widow to a High Priest should not take effect upon the prohibition of his sister.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:12:2.hebrew: רבנן היא - דאמרי: איסור חל על איסור. הילכך, איצטריך להו למילף דה"מ איסור חמור על איסור קל, אבל קל על חמור — לא חייל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:12:2.english: It is the Rabbis - Who say [that] a prohibition takes effect upon a prohibition. Therefore, it was necessary for them to derive that this statement applies to a severe prohibition upon a light prohibition, but a light [prohibition] upon a severe [prohibition] does not take effect.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:13:1.hebrew: איסור כהונה שאני - שריבה בהן הכתוב מצות יתירות, הילכך אפילו קל על חמור דעלמא ליחול — קא משמע לן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:13:1.english: A prohibition involving the priesthood is different - For Scripture multiplied additional commandments for them; therefore, even a light [prohibition] should take effect upon an ordinary severe [one] — [so it] teaches us [that it does not take effect].

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:14:1.hebrew: זונה משוי לה - פשיטא ליה דזונה משוי לה, דהא נבעלה בעילת פסול, ואסורה לכהן משום זונה. אלא הא מיבעיא לי: חללה מי משוי לה — ללקות כהן עליה משום חללה — או לא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:14:1.english: He makes her a zona - It is obvious to him that he makes her a zona, for she engaged in a disqualified intercourse and is forbidden to a priest as a zona. Rather, this is what he is asking: Does he make her a ḥalala — so that a priest would incur lashes on her account for [violating the prohibition of] a ḥalala — or not?

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:16:1.hebrew: לכ"ג מיבעיא - מהדיוטותו נאסרה עליו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:16:1.english: Is it necessary [to state regarding] a High Priest - From his [status as a] common priest, she was [already] forbidden to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:16:2.hebrew: כשם שחלוקה גרושה מזונה וחללה - האמורות אצל כהן הדיוט, שייחד לה לאו לעצמה: "ואשה גרושה מאישה לא יקחו" (ויקרא כ״א:ז׳), ללמדך שאם זונה וחללה וגרושה היא, לוקה עליה אף משום גרושה — כך חלוקה בכ"ג, אע"פ שנאמרו (לו) בו בלאו אחד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:16:2.english: Just as a divorcée is distinct from a zona and a ḥalala - [Which are] stated regarding a common priest, where [Scripture] designated a negative prohibition for her by itself: “Neither shall they take a woman divorced from her husband” (Leviticus 21:7), to teach you that if she is a zona and a ḥalala and a divorcée, he is flogged for her also on account of [her being] a divorcée — so too, she is distinct in [the case of] a High Priest, even though they were stated regarding him in a single negative prohibition.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:17:1.hebrew: פשיטא מיגרע גרע - בתמיה: וכי מפני שנעשה כ"ג נתמעטה קדושתו? הלא מהדיוטותו נחלקה עליו לשני לאוין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:17:1.english: This is obvious; is [his status] any lower? - [This is said] in astonishment: Did his sanctity diminish because he became a High Priest? Surely from [the time of] his [status as a] common priest it was [already] divided for him into two negative commandments!

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:17:2.hebrew: איתוסף בה איסור גרושה אצל כ"ג - ואע"פ שאסורה לו כבר, ומיחייב שתים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:17:2.english: The prohibition of a divorcée was added to her regarding a High Priest - And even though she was already forbidden to him, he is liable for two [sets of lashes].

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:17:3.hebrew: הואיל ושם זנות פוסל אפי' בישראל - כגון אם זינתה תחתיו, נאסרת על בעלה. הכא נמי, אע"ג דהאי זנות לאו תחת בעלה הוא, מיהו שם זנות אשכחן ביה מוסיף בעלמא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:17:3.english: Since the designation of zenut disqualifies even in the case of an Israelite - For example, if she committed adultery while under him [her husband], she becomes forbidden to her husband. Here too, even though this zenut is not [committed] under her husband, nevertheless, regarding the designation of zenut, we find that it constitutes an expanded [prohibition] in general.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:17:4.hebrew: כך חלוקה אלמנה מגרושה כו' - שאם היתה אלמנה וגרושה וחללה זונה, חייב על כל אחת ואחת. והאי דנקט תנא לפלוגי אלמנה לחודה, ולא איצטריך לפלוגי חללה מזונה — משום דחללה דמוחלקת מזונה, מכהן הדיוט קים לן, דגלי בגרושה וה"ה בחללה; אבל אלמנה, דאיתוספא בכ"ג ולא מצינו בה שנתחלקה, איצטריך ליה למילף:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:17:4.english: So too, a widow is distinct from a divorcée, etc. - That if she was a widow, and a divorcée, and a ḥalala, [and] a zona, he is liable for each and every one. And as for that which the Tanna formulated [the teaching] to distinguish a widow alone, and did not need to distinguish a ḥalala from a zona — [this is] because that a ḥalala is distinct from a zona is established for us from [the case of] a common priest, for [the Torah] revealed [this distinction] regarding a divorcée, and the same applies to a ḥalala; but a widow, which was added [only] in the case of a High Priest and we did not find regarding her that she was distinguished [elsewhere], he needed to derive [it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:18:1.hebrew: חללה למה נאמרה - הרי אסורה לכהן הדיוט! לומר לך: אין חללה אלא מאיסור כהונה. מקרא יתירה דרשי', דהאי דהדר כתבה, להכי כתבה — לומר שתלמד מסדר האמור: חללה אחר אלמנה וגרושה, שאין איסורן נוהג אלא בכהנים, ולא כתבה אחר זונה, שמצינו שם זנות פוסל בישראל — לומר לך שאין נקראת חללה אלא מביאת פסול כהונה לבדה, ולא מביאת איסור הנוהג אף בישראל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:18:1.english: Why is a chalalah stated? - Behold, she is [already] forbidden to a common priest! [It is stated] to tell you: A chalalah [results] only from a prohibition of the priesthood. We expound [this from] a superfluous verse, for the fact that [the Torah] reiterated it was written for this [purpose]: to say that you should learn from the order of what is stated — [namely,] “chalalah” [appears] after “widow” and “divorcee,” whose prohibitions apply only to priests, and it did not write it after “zona,” where we find that the designation of zenut disqualifies among Israelites — to tell you that [a woman] is called a chalalah only from an act of intercourse of a priestly disqualification alone, and not from an act of intercourse of a prohibition that applies to Israelites as well.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:18:2.english: And it is stated there - With regard to a common priest.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:18:3.hebrew: מה כאן - בכ"ג, זרעו חולין, דכתיב: "לא יחלל":
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:18:3.english: Just as here - In [the case of] a High Priest, his offspring are profaned, as it is written: "He shall not profane [his offspring]" (Leviticus 21:15).

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:19:1.english: Consequently - Since [a woman becomes] a ḥalala only through a prohibition [specific to the] priesthood.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:19:2.hebrew: כהן - הדיוט או כ"ג שבא על אחותו פנויה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:19:2.english: A priest - [Whether an] ordinary [priest] or a High Priest who engaged in intercourse with his unmarried sister.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:3:1.hebrew: נזיר שהיה שותה וכו' - וכל הני חייב, במלקות קא מיירי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:3:1.english: A nazirite who was drinking, etc. - And all of these [instances of] "liable" are speaking of lashes.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:4:1.english: No, it is necessary - That he engaged in a single act of intercourse with Reuven’s widow who had been, etc.:

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:6:1.hebrew: איסור מוסיף אית ליה - שהוא חל על איסור. כשהאיסור השני מוסיף עליה לאוסרה במה שהיתה מותרת לו מחמת איסור ראשון, אית ליה שהוא חל, אע"פ שהיתה אסורה לו מחמת איסור ראשון, להתחייב שתים. הילכך, בזמן שהן כסדר, יש בכולן איסור מוסיף, כדמפרש ואזיל: אלמנה לא היתה אסורה לכהן הדיוט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:6:1.english: He holds [the principle of] an expanded prohibition - That it takes effect upon [an existing] prohibition. When the second prohibition adds upon her, to forbid her in that which was permitted to him under the first prohibition, he holds that it takes effect — even though she was [already] forbidden to him on account of the first prohibition — to [render him] liable for two [sets of lashes]. Therefore, when they occur in order, each of them involves an expanded prohibition, as [the Gemara] proceeds to explain: A widow was not forbidden to a common priest.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:7:1.hebrew: נתגרשה מגו דאיתוסף עלה - מחמת שם גרושה איסור אצל הדיוט, שהיתה מותרת לו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:7:1.english: [Once] she was divorced, since [a prohibition] was added to her - On account of the status of a divorcée, a prohibition with regard to a common priest, to whom she had been permitted.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:7:2.hebrew: איתוסף בה איסור גרושה אצל כ"ג - ואע"פ שאסורה לו כבר, ומיחייב שתים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:7:2.english: The prohibition of a divorcée is added to her with regard to a High Priest - Even though she was already forbidden to him, and he is [now] liable for two [sets of lashes].

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:7:3.english: To partake of teruma - If she is the daughter of a priest.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:7:4.hebrew: מגו דאיתוסף בה איסורא - משום חללה למיכל בתרומה, כדילפינן מ"לא יחלל", דנתחללה מקדושתה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:7:4.english: Since a prohibition was added to her - [Namely,] on account of [her status as a] ḥalala, [forbidding her] to eat teruma, as we derive from "He shall not profane" [Leviticus 21:15], that she has been profaned from her sanctity.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:7:5.hebrew: איתוסף בה איסור לגבי כ"ג - ללקות אף משום חללה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:7:5.english: A prohibition was added to her with regard to a High Priest - To receive lashes also on account of [the prohibition of] a ḥalala.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:8:1.hebrew: מאי איסור מוסיף אית בה - במה נאסרה משום זה, שלא נאסרה קודם לכן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:8:1.english: What expanded prohibition is there with regard to her - In what respect was she forbidden on account of this that she was not forbidden beforehand?

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:8:2.hebrew: הואיל ושם זנות פוסל אפי' בישראל - כגון אם זינתה תחתיו, נאסרת על בעלה. הכא נמי, אע"ג דהאי זנות לאו תחת בעלה הוא — מיהו שם זנות אשכחן ביה מוסיף בעלמא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:8:2.english: Since the label of zenut disqualifies even regarding an Israelite - For example, if she committed adultery under him [her husband], she is forbidden to her husband. Here too, even though this zenut is not under her husband, nevertheless, we find that the label of zenut is an added prohibition in general.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:9:1.hebrew: כל שהוא ביקח - והוא: ״אשה בבתוליה יקח״, וסמיך ליה: ״אלמנה וגרושה וחללה זונה לא יקח״. כל שאתה קורא בה, כשהיא בתולה, ״יקח״ — דראויה לכ"ג — ישנו ב״בל יקח״, אם היתה אלמנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:9:1.english: Any [woman] who is in "shall he take" - And that is: "A woman in her virginity shall he take" [Leviticus 21:13], and adjacent to it: "A widow, and a divorcée, and a profaned woman, [or] a harlot, shall he not take" [Leviticus 21:14]. Any [woman] concerning whom you read, when she is a virgin, "shall he take" — as she is fit for a High Priest — is subject to "shall he not take" if she was a widow.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:9:2.hebrew: פרט לכ"ג וכו' - שאינו לוקה עליה משום איסור כהונה, אלא משום איסור אחותו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77b:9:2.english: This excludes a High Priest, etc. - That he does not receive lashes on her account due to the prohibition of priesthood, but rather due to the prohibition of his sister.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 77b:1:1.hebrew: הרי גופים מוחלקים ושמות מוחלקים - נראה דבכדי נקט "שמות מוחלקין", שהרי בא על שלשה נשים נדות בהעלם אחת חייב על כל אחת ואחת, ואע"פ שהן שם אחד — כלומר, שכולן נשים לאיש אחד — כדמפרש [בכריתות פ"ג] (דף טו.). אלא האי דנקט ג' אלמנות של ג' בני אדם — לאו דוקא, דה"ה ג' אלמנות של אדם אחד. וכן משמע מדמשני: "אלא שבא על אלמנה אחת ג' ביאות", ולא משני שבא על שלשה אלמנות של אדם אחד; מכלל דכה"ג חייב שלשה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 77b:1:1.english: Aren’t they separate bodies and separate designations - It appears that [the Gemara] mentioned "separate designations" [shemot muḥlakin] needlessly, for one who engages in intercourse with three menstruant women in a single lapse of awareness is liable for each and every one, even though they are a single designation — that is to say, [even when] they are all wives of one man — as is explained in Keritot, chapter 3 (15a). Rather, that which [the Gemara] mentioned "three widows of three men" was not precise, for the same would apply to three widows of one man. And this is also indicated by [the Gemara's] answer: "Rather, [it refers to a case] where he engaged in three acts of intercourse with one widow," and it does not answer that he engaged in intercourse with three widows of one man; from which it follows that in such a case, he is [indeed] liable for three [sets of lashes].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 77b:9:1.hebrew: פרט לכ"ג שבא על אחותו אלמנה - תימה: מאי קאמר בסמוך דרבי שמעון לית ליה איסור חל על איסור? אימא: דאיסור חל על איסור לית ליה, איסור מוסיף אית ליה! והאי איסורא מוסיף הוא גבי אחותו — שהרי מעיקרא היה האיסור משום אחותו, וכשנתאלמנה איתוסף בה איסור אלמנה [דהוי איסור מוסיף לגבי משוח מלחמה שאינו אחיו, וכל הנשים האסורות לכ"ג אסורות אף למשוח מלחמה]. וי"ל, דאיתא בברייתא אחרת דרבי שמעון אפילו איסור מוסיף לית ליה. א"נ יש לומר, דהכי מייתי: כיון דר"ש לית ליה איסור חל על איסור, ואע"ג דהוי איסור חמור על איסור קל — כי ההיא דאוכל נבילה ביום הכפורים, דלא חל איסור יום הכפורים שהיא בכרת על איסור נבלה שהיא בלאו — הכי אית לן למימר, דלית ליה איסור מוסיף באיסור קל על איסור חמור, כי ההיא דכ"ג שבא על אחותו אלמנה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 77b:9:1.english: This excludes a High Priest who engaged in intercourse with his widowed sister - It is puzzling: Why does [the Gemara] say nearby that Rabbi Shimon holds that a prohibition does not take effect upon [another] prohibition? Say that [while] he does not hold that a prohibition takes effect upon [another] prohibition, he does hold that an expanded prohibition [takes effect]! And this is an expanded prohibition with regard to his sister, as initially the prohibition was due to [her being] his sister, and when she became widowed, the prohibition of a widow was added to her [as it is an expanded prohibition with regard to a priest anointed for war who is not her brother, and all women forbidden to a High Priest are also forbidden to a priest anointed for war]. And it can be answered that it is found in another baraita that Rabbi Shimon does not hold even [the principle of] an expanded prohibition. Alternatively, it can be answered that this is how [Rav Sheshet] brings [his proof]: Since Rabbi Shimon holds that a prohibition does not take effect upon [another] prohibition, even though it is a severe prohibition upon a light prohibition — like that [case] of one who eats a carcass on Yom Kippur, where the prohibition of Yom Kippur, which carries [the penalty of] karet, does not take effect upon the prohibition of a carcass, which is [punishable only] by a negative commandment — so too we must say that he does not hold that an expanded prohibition [takes effect in the case of] a light prohibition upon a severe prohibition, like that [case] of a High Priest who engaged in intercourse with his widowed sister.
